# Tasks: [FEATURE NAME]

**Input**: Design documents from `/specs/[###-feature-name]/`

**Prerequisites**: plan.md (required), spec.md (required for user stories), research.md, data-model.md, contracts/

**Tests**: The examples below include test tasks. Tests are OPTIONAL - only include them if explicitly requested in the feature specification.

**Organization**: Tasks are grouped by user story to enable independent implementation and testing of each story.

## Format: `[ID] [P?] [Story] Description`

- **[P]**: Can run in parallel (different files, no dependencies)
- **[Story]**: Which user story this task belongs to (e.g., US1, US2, US3)
- Include exact file paths in descriptions

## Path Conventions

- **Single project**: `src/`, `tests/` at repository root
- **Web app**: `backend/src/`, `frontend/src/`
- **Mobile**: `api/src/`, `ios/src/` or `android/src/`
- Paths shown below assume single project - adjust based on plan.md structure

<!--
  ============================================================================
  IMPORTANT: The tasks below are SAMPLE TASKS for illustration purposes only.

  The /speckit-tasks command MUST replace these with actual tasks based on:
  - User stories from spec.md (with their priorities P1, P2, P3...)
  - Feature requirements from plan.md
  - Entities from data-model.md
  - Endpoints from contracts/

  Tasks MUST be organized by user story so each story can be:
  - Implemented independently
  - Tested independently
  - Delivered as an MVP increment

  DO NOT keep these sample tasks in the generated tasks.md file.
  ============================================================================
-->

## Phase 1: Setup (Shared Infrastructure)

**Purpose**: Project initialization and basic structure

- [ ] T001 Create project structure per implementation plan
- [ ] T002 Initialize [language] project with [framework] dependencies
- [ ] T003 [P] Configure linting and formatting tools

---

## Phase 2: Foundational (Blocking Prerequisites)

**Purpose**: Core infrastructure that MUST be complete before ANY user story can be implemented

**⚠️ CRITICAL**: No user story work can begin until this phase is complete

Examples of foundational tasks (adjust based on your project):

- [ ] T004 Setup database schema and migrations framework
- [ ] T005 [P] Implement authentication/authorization framework
- [ ] T006 [P] Setup API routing and middleware structure
- [ ] T007 Create base models/entities that all stories depend on
- [ ] T008 Configure error handling and logging infrastructure
- [ ] T009 Setup environment configuration management

**Checkpoint**: Foundation ready - user story implementation can now begin in parallel

---

## Phase 3: User Story 1 - [Title] (Priority: P1) 🎯 MVP

**Goal**: [Brief description of what this story delivers]

**Independent Test**: [How to verify this story works on its own]

### Tests for User Story 1 (OPTIONAL - only if tests requested) ⚠️

> **NOTE: Write these tests FIRST, ensure they FAIL before implementation**

- [ ] T010 [P] [US1] Contract test for [endpoint] in tests/contract/test_[name].py
- [ ] T011 [P] [US1] Integration test for [user journey] in tests/integration/test_[name].py

### Implementation for User Story 1

- [ ] T012 [P] [US1] Create [Entity1] model in src/models/[entity1].py
- [ ] T013 [P] [US1] Create [Entity2] model in src/models/[entity2].py
- [ ] T014 [US1] Implement [Service] in src/services/[service].py (depends on T012, T013)
- [ ] T015 [US1] Implement [endpoint/feature] in src/[location]/[file].py
- [ ] T016 [US1] Add validation and error handling
- [ ] T017 [US1] Add logging for user story 1 operations

**Checkpoint**: At this point, User Story 1 should be fully functional and testable independently

---

## Phase 4: User Story 2 - [Title] (Priority: P2)

**Goal**: [Brief description of what this story delivers]

**Independent Test**: [How to verify this story works on its own]

### Tests for User Story 2 (OPTIONAL - only if tests requested) ⚠️

- [ ] T019 [P] [US2] Integration test for [user journey] in tests/integration/test_[name].py

- [ ] T023 [US2] Integrate with User Story 1 components (if needed)

**Checkpoint**: At this point, User Stories 1 AND 2 should both work independently

---

## Phase 5: User Story 3 - [Title] (Priority: P3)

**Goal**: [Brief description of what this story delivers]

**Independent Test**: [How to verify this story works on its own]

### Tests for User Story 3 (OPTIONAL - only if tests requested) ⚠️

- [ ] T024 [P] [US3] Contract test for [endpoint] in tests/contract/test_[name].py
- [ ] T025 [P] [US3] Integration test for [user journey] in tests/integration/test_[name].py

### Implementation for User Story 3

- [ ] T026 [P] [US3] Create [Entity] model in src/models/[entity].py
- [ ] T027 [US3] Implement [Service] in src/services/[service].py
- [ ] T028 [US3] Implement [endpoint/feature] in src/[location]/[file].py

**Checkpoint**: All user stories should now be independently functional

---

[Add more user story phases as needed, following the same pattern]

---

## Phase N: Polish & Cross-Cutting Concerns

**Purpose**: Improvements that affect multiple user stories

- [ ] TXXX [P] Documentation updates in docs/
- [ ] TXXX Code cleanup and refactoring
- [ ] TXXX Performance optimization across all stories
- [ ] TXXX [P] Additional unit tests (if requested) in tests/unit/
- [ ] TXXX Security hardening
- [ ] TXXX Run quickstart.md validation

---

## Dependencies & Execution Order

### Phase Dependencies

- **Setup (Phase 1)**: No dependencies - can start immediately
- **Foundational (Phase 2)**: Depends on Setup completion - BLOCKS all user stories
- **User Stories (Phase 3+)**: All depend on Foundational phase completion
  - User stories can then proceed in parallel (if staffed)
  - Or sequentially in priority order (P1 → P2 → P3)
- **Polish (Final Phase)**: Depends on all desired user stories being complete

### User Story Dependencies

- **User Story 1 (P1)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - No dependencies on other stories
- **User Story 2 (P2)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - May integrate with US1 but should be independently testable
- **User Story 3 (P3)**: Can start after Foundational (Phase 2) - May integrate with US1/US2 but should be independently testable

### Within Each User Story

- Tests (if included) MUST be written and FAIL before implementation
- Models before services
- Services before endpoints
- Core implementation before integration
- Story complete before moving to next priority

### Parallel Opportunities

- All Setup tasks marked [P] can run in parallel
- All Foundational tasks marked [P] can run in parallel (within Phase 2)
- Once Foundational phase completes, all user stories can start in parallel (if team capacity allows)
- All tests for a user story marked [P] can run in parallel
- Models within a story marked [P] can run in parallel
- Different user stories can be worked on in parallel by different team members

---

## Parallel Example: User Story 1

```bash
# Launch all tests for User Story 1 together (if tests requested):
Task: "Contract test for [endpoint] in tests/contract/test_[name].py"
Task: "Integration test for [user journey] in tests/integration/test_[name].py"

# Launch all models for User Story 1 together:
Task: "Create [Entity1] model in src/models/[entity1].py"
Task: "Create [Entity2] model in src/models/[entity2].py"
```

---

## Implementation Strategy

### MVP First (User Story 1 Only)

1. Complete Phase 1: Setup
2. Complete Phase 2: Foundational (CRITICAL - blocks all stories)
3. Complete Phase 3: User Story 1
4. **STOP and VALIDATE**: Test User Story 1 independently
5. Deploy/demo if ready

### Incremental Delivery

1. Complete Setup + Foundational → Foundation ready
2. Add User Story 1 → Test independently → Deploy/Demo (MVP!)
3. Add User Story 2 → Test independently → Deploy/Demo
4. Add User Story 3 → Test independently → Deploy/Demo
5. Each story adds value without breaking previous stories

### Parallel Team Strategy

With multiple developers:

1. Team completes Setup + Foundational together
2. Once Foundational is done:
   - Developer A: User Story 1
   - Developer B: User Story 2
   - Developer C: User Story 3
3. Stories complete and integrate independently

---

## Notes

- [P] tasks = different files, no dependencies
- [Story] label maps task to specific user story for traceability
- Each user story should be independently completable and testable
- Verify tests fail before implementing
- Commit after each task or logical group
- Stop at any checkpoint to validate story independently
- Avoid: vague tasks, same file conflicts, cross-story dependencies that break independence
"}

1	# Implementation Plan: Meeting-Room Bookings
2	
3	**Branch**: none — no branch hook is installed; the work stays on `main` (feature directory `specs/001-room-bookings`) | **Date**: 2026-11-10 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)
4	
5	**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-room-bookings/spec.md`
6	
7	**Note**: This template is filled in by the `/speckit-plan` command; its definition describes the execution workflow.
8	
9	## Summary
10	
11	Add bookings to roombook in four parts, all on the existing stack and the existing shared contract:
12	
13	1. **Bookings API** — five routes under `/api/bookings` on the gateway, which validates and forwards
14	   over NATS; the `booking` service owns the rules and two new tables.
15	2. **Idempotent create** — the key is checked by a gateway guard; the `booking` repository claims the
16	   key and inserts the booking in one transaction, using two transaction-scoped advisory locks to
17	   answer "in progress" (409) and "key reused" (422) without a stored in-progress state.
18	3. **Confirmation job** — the `booking` service enqueues one BullMQ job per created booking; the
19	   `worker` reads the booking over NATS, runs a simulated sender and reports each attempt; the
20	   `booking` service records it with one conditional update.
21	4. **Bookings page** — `/bookings` in `apps/web` with a table, room filter, create form, edit and
22	   delete dialogs, and an idempotency key that survives only a network error.
23	
24	Design decisions and their reasons are in [research.md](./research.md).
25	
26	## Technical Context
27	
28	**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.9 on Node 22 or newer
29	
30	**Primary Dependencies**: NestJS 11 (HTTP gateway, NATS microservices), TypeORM 0.3, BullMQ 5 with `@nestjs/bullmq`, class-validator / class-transformer, Next.js 15 (pages router) with React 18 and MUI 5, react-hook-form with yup, axios, uuid — all already installed; no dependency is added
31	
32	**Storage**: PostgreSQL 15 (two new tables: `bookings`, `idempotency_keys`); Redis 7.2 for the `booking-confirmation` queue
33	
34	**Testing**: Jest 29 through Nx (`pnpm run test`); `@nestjs/testing` with mocked neighbours for the backend, Testing Library with the service layer mocked for the web page
35	
36	**Target Platform**: Node services and a browser frontend, run locally through `pnpm run stack:up` (Docker for Postgres, Redis and NATS)
37	
38	**Project Type**: Web application in an Nx monorepo — HTTP gateway, NATS services, queue worker, Next.js frontend
39	
40	**Performance Goals**: every booking reaches its final confirmation state within 10 seconds of creation (SC-004); no throughput target
41	
42	**Constraints**: `libs/contract`, `apps/room` and the `/rooms` page are not changed (FR-033); no new dependency; the worker has no database access; transactions only in repositories; every code file under 200 lines; `.env` files are never read
43	
44	**Scale/Scope**: a demo system with synthetic data and no sign-in; 5 HTTP routes, 6 NATS handlers, 1 queue, 2 tables, 1 page; about 45 new source files (specs included) across `apps/gateway`, `apps/booking`, `apps/worker`, `apps/web` and `libs/backend-common`
45	
46	## Constitution Check
47	
48	*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*
49	
50	Evaluated against `.specify/memory/constitution.md` v1.0.0.
51	
52	| Principle | Gate | Result |
53	|---|---|---|
54	| I. Contract as Source of Truth | Routes, patterns, queue name, DTO classes, error codes, header names and constants all come from `@roombook/contract`. Where the contract defines no answer class (`deleteBooking`, `recordConfirmationResult`) or no job name, an existing contract export is reused; nothing is added to or changed in the contract. Errors cross boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }` through `ExceptionHelper`. | PASS |
55	| II. Layered Architecture | Gateway handlers are one forwarding statement each, following the existing `RoomController`; the key check is a guard and the replay header an interceptor. `POST` takes `CreateBookingDto`, `PATCH` takes `UpdateBookingDto`. Rules live in `booking` services, data access in repositories, and the only transaction is in `IdempotentBookingRepository`. The gateway and the worker have no database access. Each new class is registered in one module. No literal port, host, URL or secret is added; no new environment variable is needed. Health patterns for all services already exist and no deployable is added. | PASS |
56	| III. Strict TypeScript | No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object parameter types, explicit return types on every repository method, named imports only. Internal shapes (claim result, sender decision) are named classes or `type`s. | PASS |
57	| IV. Small, Self-Describing Files | Kebab-case names that state their purpose; the booking create flow, the other booking operations, the two repositories and the page's parts are split so each file stays under 200 lines; no narrative comments. | PASS |
58	| V. Test-First | Every new or modified service, repository, controller, guard, interceptor, processor, hook and component gets a `*.spec.ts(x)` next to it, written and failing before the implementation. | PASS |
59	| Safety Constraints | `.env` files are not read (configuration is referred to by name); git stays local; no dependency is added. | PASS |
60	| Quality Gates | `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` are the completion check (quickstart, "Automated gates"). | PASS |
61	
62	**Initial gate**: PASS — no violation, nothing to justify.
63	
64	**Post-design re-check** (after research, data model and contracts): PASS. Points that were checked
65	again because the design touched them:
66	
67	- The internal claim outcome (`CREATED`, `REPLAYED`, `KEY_REUSED`, `IN_PROGRESS`) is a value inside the
68	  `booking` service; it never crosses a service boundary, so it is not a contract item (Principle I).

# Implementation Plan: Meeting-Room Bookings

**Branch**: none — no branch hook is installed; the work stays on `main` (feature directory `specs/001-room-bookings`) | **Date**: 2026-11-10 | **Spec**: [spec.md](./spec.md)

**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/001-room-bookings/spec.md`

**Note**: This template is filled in by the `/speckit-plan` command; its definition describes the execution workflow.

## Summary

Add bookings to roombook in four parts, all on the existing stack and the existing shared contract:

1. **Bookings API** — five routes under `/api/bookings` on the gateway, which validates and forwards
   over NATS; the `booking` service owns the rules and two new tables.
2. **Idempotent create** — the key is checked by a gateway guard; the `booking` repository claims the
   key and inserts the booking in one transaction, using two transaction-scoped advisory locks to
   answer "in progress" (409) and "key reused" (422) without a stored in-progress state.
3. **Confirmation job** — the `booking` service enqueues one BullMQ job per created booking; the
   `worker` reads the booking over NATS, runs a simulated sender and reports each attempt; the
   `booking` service records it with one conditional update.
4. **Bookings page** — `/bookings` in `apps/web` with a table, room filter, create form, edit and
   delete dialogs, and an idempotency key that survives only a network error.

Design decisions and their reasons are in [research.md](./research.md).

## Technical Context

**Language/Version**: TypeScript 5.9 on Node 22 or newer

**Primary Dependencies**: NestJS 11 (HTTP gateway, NATS microservices), TypeORM 0.3, BullMQ 5 with `@nestjs/bullmq`, class-validator / class-transformer, Next.js 15 (pages router) with React 18 and MUI 5, react-hook-form with yup, axios, uuid — all already installed; no dependency is added

**Storage**: PostgreSQL 15 (two new tables: `bookings`, `idempotency_keys`); Redis 7.2 for the `booking-confirmation` queue

**Testing**: Jest 29 through Nx (`pnpm run test`); `@nestjs/testing` with mocked neighbours for the backend, Testing Library with the service layer mocked for the web page

**Target Platform**: Node services and a browser frontend, run locally through `pnpm run stack:up` (Docker for Postgres, Redis and NATS)

**Project Type**: Web application in an Nx monorepo — HTTP gateway, NATS services, queue worker, Next.js frontend

**Performance Goals**: every booking reaches its final confirmation state within 10 seconds of creation (SC-004); no throughput target

**Constraints**: `libs/contract`, `apps/room` and the `/rooms` page are not changed (FR-033); no new dependency; the worker has no database access; transactions only in repositories; every code file under 200 lines; `.env` files are never read

**Scale/Scope**: a demo system with synthetic data and no sign-in; 5 HTTP routes, 6 NATS handlers, 1 queue, 2 tables, 1 page; about 45 new source files (specs included) across `apps/gateway`, `apps/booking`, `apps/worker`, `apps/web` and `libs/backend-common`

## Constitution Check

*GATE: Must pass before Phase 0 research. Re-check after Phase 1 design.*

Evaluated against `.specify/memory/constitution.md` v1.0.0.

| Principle | Gate | Result |
|---|---|---|
| I. Contract as Source of Truth | Routes, patterns, queue name, DTO classes, error codes, header names and constants all come from `@roombook/contract`. Where the contract defines no answer class (`deleteBooking`, `recordConfirmationResult`) or no job name, an existing contract export is reused; nothing is added to or changed in the contract. Errors cross boundaries as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }` through `ExceptionHelper`. | PASS |
| II. Layered Architecture | Gateway handlers are one forwarding statement each, following the existing `RoomController`; the key check is a guard and the replay header an interceptor. `POST` takes `CreateBookingDto`, `PATCH` takes `UpdateBookingDto`. Rules live in `booking` services, data access in repositories, and the only transaction is in `IdempotentBookingRepository`. The gateway and the worker have no database access. Each new class is registered in one module. No literal port, host, URL or secret is added; no new environment variable is needed. Health patterns for all services already exist and no deployable is added. | PASS |
| III. Strict TypeScript | No `interface`, no `any`, no inline object parameter types, explicit return types on every repository method, named imports only. Internal shapes (claim result, sender decision) are named classes or `type`s. | PASS |
| IV. Small, Self-Describing Files | Kebab-case names that state their purpose; the booking create flow, the other booking operations, the two repositories and the page's parts are split so each file stays under 200 lines; no narrative comments. | PASS |
| V. Test-First | Every new or modified service, repository, controller, guard, interceptor, processor, hook and component gets a `*.spec.ts(x)` next to it, written and failing before the implementation. | PASS |
| Safety Constraints | `.env` files are not read (configuration is referred to by name); git stays local; no dependency is added. | PASS |
| Quality Gates | `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` are the completion check (quickstart, "Automated gates"). | PASS |

**Initial gate**: PASS — no violation, nothing to justify.

**Post-design re-check** (after research, data model and contracts): PASS. Points that were checked
again because the design touched them:

- The internal claim outcome (`CREATED`, `REPLAYED`, `KEY_REUSED`, `IN_PROGRESS`) is a value inside the
  `booking` service; it never crosses a service boundary, so it is not a contract item (Principle I).
- The conditional updates for the time pair and the confirmation outcome are single statements in the
  repository; the service still decides the answer and its error code (Principle II).
- Moving `isErrorResponse` to its own exported file changes `libs/backend-common`, which is not a
  frozen area, and keeps the filter's behaviour (its spec stays green).

1	# Feature Specification: Meeting-Room Bookings
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: none — no branch hook is installed; the work stays on `main` (feature directory `specs/001-room-bookings`)
4	
5	**Created**: 2026-11-10
6	
7	**Status**: Draft
8	
9	**Input**: User description: "Add bookings to roombook: people book a meeting room for a time span, and get a confirmation." The description has four parts — a bookings API on the gateway, idempotent create, a confirmation job, and a `/bookings` page — plus a scope limit (the shared contract, the `room` service and the `/rooms` page are not changed) and a definition of done. Every rule it states is carried into this specification.
10	
11	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
12	
13	### User Story 1 - Book a room and manage the booking (Priority: P1)
14	
15	A person books a meeting room for a time span by giving the room, a title, the organizer's email, a start and an end. They can list bookings (all, or for one room), read one, change its title or times, and delete it.
16	
17	**Why this priority**: Bookings are the feature. Every other story depends on a booking existing.
18	
19	**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create a booking for an existing room, list it, read it, change its end time, delete it, and confirm that reading it afterwards answers "not found".
20	
21	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
22	
23	1. **Given** an existing room, **When** a valid booking is created with a valid `Idempotency-Key`, **Then** the answer is 201 with the booking, whose `confirmationStatus` is `PENDING` and `confirmationAttempts` is 0.
24	2. **Given** bookings in several rooms, **When** the list is requested without `roomId`, **Then** the answer is `{ items, total, page, limit }` with all bookings ordered by `startsAt` ascending, 10 per page by default.
25	3. **Given** bookings in several rooms, **When** the list is requested with a `roomId`, **Then** only that room's bookings are counted and returned.
26	4. **Given** an existing booking, **When** it is read by id, **Then** the answer is 200 with the booking.
27	5. **Given** no booking with that id, **When** it is read, updated or deleted, **Then** the answer is 404 with `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`.
28	6. **Given** an existing booking, **When** its `title`, `startsAt` and/or `endsAt` are changed, **Then** the answer is 200 with the updated booking and a later `updatedAt`.
29	7. **Given** an existing booking, **When** it is deleted, **Then** the answer is 204 and reading it afterwards answers 404 with `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`.
30	8. **Given** a body with a missing or malformed field, **When** a create or update is requested, **Then** the answer is 400 and nothing is stored.
31	9. **Given** `endsAt` equal to or earlier than `startsAt`, **When** a booking is created, **Then** the answer is 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`.
32	10. **Given** an existing booking, **When** an update changes only one of the two times so that the stored pair would no longer have `endsAt` later than `startsAt`, **Then** the answer is 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` and the booking is unchanged.
33	11. **Given** a `roomId` that matches no room, **When** a booking is created, **Then** the answer is 404 with `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` and nothing is stored.
34	
35	---
36	
37	### User Story 2 - Retry a create safely (Priority: P2)
38	
39	A client that is unsure whether its create request arrived can send it again with the same `Idempotency-Key` and never ends up with two bookings.
40	
41	**Why this priority**: Without it, a network error during create leaves the client a choice between a possible duplicate and a possible lost booking.
42	
43	**Independent Test**: Send the same create request twice with one key and observe one booking and an identical second answer marked as replayed; then vary the body, the key and the timing to observe each documented error.
44	
45	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
46	
47	1. **Given** a create request without an `Idempotency-Key` header, or with a value that is not a UUID, **When** it is sent, **Then** the answer is 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` and nothing is stored.
48	2. **Given** a key that has not been used, **When** a valid create is sent, **Then** the booking is created and the key, a fingerprint of the request body and the response are stored together with it, all or nothing.
49	3. **Given** a completed create, **When** the same key is sent with the same body, **Then** the stored status and body are answered unchanged with the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, no second booking exists and no second confirmation job is enqueued.
50	4. **Given** a completed create, **When** the booking is later updated or deleted and the same key and body are sent again, **Then** the originally stored answer is still returned unchanged.
51	5. **Given** a completed create, **When** the same key is sent with a different body, **Then** the answer is 422 with `UNPROCESSABLE.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.
52	6. **Given** a create that is still being processed, **When** the same key arrives again, **Then** the answer is 409 with `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`.
53	7. **Given** two identical create requests with the same key arriving at the same moment, **When** both are processed, **Then** exactly one booking exists; the other request is answered with either the replay or the 409.
54	8. **Given** a create that failed validation (invalid body, `endsAt` not later than `startsAt`, or unknown room), **When** the same key is sent again with a corrected body, **Then** it is treated as a first request and the booking is created.
55	9. **Given** a key used long ago, **When** it is sent again, **Then** it behaves exactly as above: keys do not expire.
56	
57	---
58	
59	### User Story 3 - Get a confirmation (Priority: P3)
60	
61	After a booking is created, the organizer is "sent" a confirmation in the background, and the booking shows whether that succeeded and how many attempts it took.
62	
63	**Why this priority**: It completes the promise "and get a confirmation", but a booking is already usable without it.
64	
65	**Independent Test**: Create three bookings whose organizer addresses are an ordinary one, one at `@retry.example` and one at `@bounce.example`; after the retries have run, read each booking and compare its status and attempts with the fixed rules.
66	
67	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
68	
69	1. **Given** a newly created booking, **When** creation completes, **Then** exactly one confirmation job for that booking is on the `booking-confirmation` queue, with payload `{ bookingId }`, the job id `confirmationJobId(bookingId)`, 3 attempts and exponential backoff starting at 1 second.
70	2. **Given** an organizer address in any ordinary domain, **When** the job runs, **Then** the booking ends as `SENT` with 1 attempt.
71	3. **Given** an organizer address ending in `@retry.example`, **When** the job runs, **Then** the first two attempts fail, the third succeeds, and the booking ends as `SENT` with 3 attempts.
72	4. **Given** an organizer address ending in `@bounce.example`, **When** the job runs, **Then** every attempt fails and after the third the booking ends as `FAILED` with 3 attempts.
73	5. **Given** a booking whose confirmation already ended as `SENT` or `FAILED`, **When** the processor runs again for the same booking, **Then** the booking's status and attempts are unchanged.
74	6. **Given** the same attempt outcome is reported twice, **When** the second report arrives, **Then** the booking is in the same state as after the first.
75	7. **Given** a replayed create (User Story 2), **When** it is answered, **Then** the booking still has exactly one confirmation job.
76	
77	---
78	
79	### User Story 4 - Manage bookings from the web page (Priority: P4)
80	
81	A person opens the Bookings page from the navigation, sees the bookings in a table, filters them by room, creates a booking with a form, and edits or deletes a row.
82	
83	**Why this priority**: It is the human-facing surface of stories 1–3 and needs them to exist first.
84	
85	**Independent Test**: With the service layer mocked, render the page and exercise the table, the filter, the create form, edit, delete, and the loading, empty and error states. Against a running system, do the same by hand at `/bookings`.
86	
87	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
88	
89	1. **Given** any page of the app, **When** the navigation is shown, **Then** it has a "Bookings" link that opens `/bookings`.
90	2. **Given** bookings exist, **When** the page loads, **Then** a table shows for each booking its title, room name, organizer, start, end and confirmation status.
91	3. **Given** the room list, **When** a room is chosen in the filter above the table, **Then** the table shows only that room's bookings; clearing the filter shows all of them again.
92	4. **Given** the create form filled with room, title, organizer email, start and end, **When** it is submitted successfully, **Then** the new booking appears in the table.
93	5. **Given** a submission that ended in a network error (no answer from the API), **When** the person retries the same submission, **Then** the request carries the same `Idempotency-Key` as the first try.
94	6. **Given** a submission that the API answered, successfully or with an error, **When** the form is submitted again, **Then** that is a new submission with a new `Idempotency-Key`.
95	7. **Given** a row, **When** its title, start or end is edited and saved, **Then** the row shows the updated values.
96	8. **Given** a row, **When** it is deleted and the deletion is confirmed, **Then** the row disappears from the table.
97	9. **Given** bookings are being fetched, **When** the page is shown, **Then** a loading state is visible.
98	10. **Given** there are no bookings (or none for the chosen room), **When** the page loads, **Then** an empty state is shown instead of an empty table.
99	11. **Given** the API answers an error to a load, create, edit or delete, **When** the page shows the failure, **Then** it shows the `message` from the API's error answer.
100	
101	---
102	
103	### Edge Cases
104	
105	- **Header and body both invalid on create**: the idempotency key is checked first, so the answer is 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`.
106	- **Same key, different body, first request still in progress**: the body mismatch wins, so the answer is 422 with `UNPROCESSABLE.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.
107	- **Update with an empty body**: answered 200 with the booking unchanged.
108	- **Update that tries to change `roomId` or `organizerEmail`**: answered 400; only `title`, `startsAt` and `endsAt` can be changed.
109	- **An id in the path that is not a UUID**: answered 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`.
110	- **`page` below 1, `limit` below 1 or above 100, or a `roomId` filter that is not a UUID**: answered 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`.
111	- **A `roomId` filter for a room that does not exist**: answered 200 with an empty list; the filter does not check the room.
112	- **Two bookings for the same room at overlapping times**: both are accepted; this feature has no overlap rule.
113	- **A booking in the past**: accepted.
114	- **Booking deleted before its confirmation job runs or finishes**: the job ends quietly without further retries, and a late outcome report for the missing booking changes nothing.
115	- **The `room` service does not answer during create**: answered with `UNAVAILABLE.SERVICE`; nothing is stored and the key can be used again.
116	- **The queue is unreachable right after the booking is stored**: the create still answers 201 and the booking stays `PENDING`; recovering such a booking is outside this feature.
117	- **The form is edited after a network error**: the edited form is a new submission and gets a new `Idempotency-Key`.
118	- **More than one page of bookings on the web page**: the table offers paging at 10 per page.
119	
120	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
121	
122	### Functional Requirements
123	
124	**Bookings (gateway, under `/api`)**
125	
126	- **FR-001**: The system MUST expose a booking as `id`, `roomId`, `title`, `organizerEmail`, `startsAt`, `endsAt`, `confirmationStatus` (`PENDING`, `SENT` or `FAILED`), `confirmationAttempts`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, with every time in ISO 8601 UTC.
127	- **FR-002**: `POST /api/bookings` MUST create a booking and answer 201 with it; a new booking MUST start with `confirmationStatus` `PENDING` and `confirmationAttempts` 0.
128	- **FR-003**: `GET /api/bookings` MUST answer `{ items, total, page, limit }` ordered by `startsAt` ascending, with `page` defaulting to 1, `limit` defaulting to 10 (maximum 100), and an optional `roomId` that restricts both `items` and `total` to that room.
129	- **FR-004**: `GET /api/bookings/:id` MUST answer 200 with the booking, or 404 with `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`.
130	- **FR-005**: `PATCH /api/bookings/:id` MUST change only `title`, `startsAt` and/or `endsAt` and answer 200 with the updated booking, or 404 with `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`.
131	- **FR-006**: `DELETE /api/bookings/:id` MUST answer 204, or 404 with `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`; a deleted booking MUST be gone, so that reading it afterwards answers 404.
132	- **FR-007**: Every error MUST be answered as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }` with `errorCode` taken from the shared contract.
133	- **FR-008**: An invalid body MUST be answered with 400 and store nothing. A title is 1 to 120 characters, `organizerEmail` is an email address, `roomId` is a UUID, and both times are strict ISO 8601.
134	- **FR-009**: `endsAt` MUST be later than `startsAt`; equal or earlier MUST be answered with 400 and `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`. After an update, the rule MUST hold for the resulting stored pair of times, including when only one of them was sent.
135	- **FR-010**: The room of a new booking MUST exist. The `booking` service MUST ask the `room` service, and an unknown room MUST be answered with 404 and `NOT_FOUND.ROOM`.
136	- **FR-011**: The `booking` service MUST own bookings and their storage. The gateway MUST only validate and forward; it holds no booking rules and no storage.
137	
138	**Idempotent create**
139	
140	- **FR-012**: `POST /api/bookings` MUST require the `Idempotency-Key` request header with a UUID value; a missing or non-UUID value MUST be answered with 400 and `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`.
141	- **FR-013**: On the first request with a key, the system MUST store the key, a fingerprint of the request body, and the response. Claiming the key and inserting the booking MUST happen in one database transaction.
142	- **FR-014**: The same key with the same body, after the first request completed, MUST be answered with the stored status and body, unchanged, plus the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; it MUST NOT create a second booking or enqueue a second confirmation job.
143	- **FR-015**: The same key with a different body MUST be answered with 422 and `UNPROCESSABLE.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.
144	- **FR-016**: The same key while the first request is still being processed MUST be answered with 409 and `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`.
145	- **FR-017**: Two identical requests arriving at the same moment MUST never create two bookings.
146	- **FR-018**: A request that fails validation (FR-008, FR-009, FR-010) MUST NOT be stored against its key; the key MUST remain usable.
147	- **FR-019**: Idempotency keys MUST NOT expire.
148	
149	**Confirmation job**
150	
151	- **FR-020**: When a booking is created, the `booking` service MUST enqueue exactly one confirmation job on the queue `booking-confirmation` with payload `{ bookingId }`.
152	- **FR-021**: The job id MUST be `confirmationJobId(bookingId)`, so that a booking can never have two confirmation jobs.
153	- **FR-022**: The job MUST be given 3 attempts with exponential backoff starting at 1 second.
154	- **FR-023**: The `worker` service MUST process the job: it "sends" the confirmation and reports the outcome to the `booking` service over the message bus, and the `booking` service MUST update the booking's `confirmationStatus` and `confirmationAttempts`. The worker MUST NOT have database access.
155	- **FR-024**: Nothing MUST really be sent. The simulated sender MUST decide by the booking's `organizerEmail`:
156	  - ending in `@retry.example`: fail on attempts 1 and 2, succeed on attempt 3 — the booking ends as `SENT` with 3 attempts;
157	  - ending in `@bounce.example`: fail on every attempt — after the third the booking ends as `FAILED` with 3 attempts;
158	  - any other address: succeed on attempt 1 — `SENT` with 1 attempt.
159	- **FR-025**: The processor MUST be safe to run twice for the same booking: a repeated run or a repeated outcome report MUST NOT change a booking that already ended as `SENT` or `FAILED`, and MUST NOT lower `confirmationAttempts`.
160	
161	**Bookings page (`apps/web`)**
162	
163	- **FR-026**: The web app MUST have a `/bookings` page and a "Bookings" link in the navigation.
164	- **FR-027**: The page MUST show a table of bookings with title, room name, organizer, start, end and confirmation status.
165	- **FR-028**: The page MUST have a room filter above the table, filled from the room list.
166	- **FR-029**: The page MUST have a form to create a booking with room, title, organizer email, start and end.
167	- **FR-030**: Each form submission MUST generate one `Idempotency-Key`; a retry of the same submission after a network error MUST reuse that key.
168	- **FR-031**: Each row MUST offer edit (title, start, end) and delete.
169	- **FR-032**: The page MUST have loading, empty and error states; an error MUST show the `message` from the API.
170	
171	**Scope and completion**
172	
173	- **FR-033**: The shared contract (`libs/contract`), the `room` service and the `/rooms` page MUST NOT be changed. Every route name, message pattern, DTO class, error code, header name, queue name and constant MUST come from the shared contract as it is.
174	- **FR-034**: New and changed services MUST have unit tests, and the page MUST have tests with the service layer mocked.
175	- **FR-035**: `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` MUST pass.
176	
177	### Key Entities
178	
179	- **Booking**: one reservation of one room for a time span. Holds the room it is for, a title, the organizer's email, start and end, the state of its confirmation (status and number of attempts), and when it was created and last updated. Belongs to exactly one room; owned by the `booking` service.
180	- **Room**: an existing meeting room with a name and a capacity. Read-only for this feature; owned by the `room` service.
181	- **Idempotency record**: one per `Idempotency-Key`. Holds the key, the fingerprint of the request body it was first used with, whether that request is still in progress or completed, and the stored response (status and body). Never expires.
182	- **Confirmation job**: one background task per booking, identified by the booking, that drives the simulated sending with up to 3 attempts.
183	- **Confirmation outcome**: the report the worker gives the `booking` service after an attempt: the booking, the resulting status, and the attempt count.
184	
185	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
186	
187	### Measurable Outcomes
188	
189	- **SC-001**: A person can create, find, change and delete a booking, and 100% of the documented answers (success and error) match this specification when exercised end to end through the gateway.
190	- **SC-002**: Sending the same create request with the same key any number of times, one after another or at the same moment, results in exactly 1 booking and exactly 1 confirmation job, in 100% of trials.
191	- **SC-003**: Every replayed answer is identical in status and body to the original answer and is marked as replayed.
192	- **SC-004**: With the default retry timing, every booking reaches its final confirmation state within 10 seconds of creation: ordinary address `SENT` with 1 attempt, `@retry.example` `SENT` with 3 attempts, `@bounce.example` `FAILED` with 3 attempts.
193	- **SC-005**: Running the confirmation processor a second time for any booking leaves its status and attempts unchanged in 100% of trials.
194	- **SC-006**: On the Bookings page a person can create a booking in under 1 minute and can filter, edit and delete without leaving the page; every failure shows the API's own message.
195	- **SC-007**: The repository's build, lint and test commands all pass, and the `room` service, the `/rooms` page and the shared contract show no changes.
196	
197	## Assumptions
198	
199	- **No sign-in**: roombook has no authentication, so anyone who can reach the gateway or the page can create, change and delete any booking.
200	- **No overlap rule**: the description does not forbid two bookings of one room at the same time and the contract has no error code for it, so overlapping bookings are accepted.
201	- **Past bookings**: start and end may be in the past.
202	- **Invalid body error code**: "an invalid body answers 400" is answered with `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`, the only general validation code in the contract. The same code is used for an invalid list query or a path id that is not a UUID.
203	- **"Fails validation" includes the room check**: the unknown-room answer is listed under validation in the description, so a 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` create is not stored against its key either.
204	- **"Same body"**: two bodies are the same when the five create fields (`roomId`, `title`, `organizerEmail`, `startsAt`, `endsAt`) have the same values; field order and whitespace in the JSON do not matter.
205	- **Mismatch before in-progress**: when a key is reused with a different body, the 422 applies whether or not the first request has completed.
206	- **Replay is a snapshot**: a replay returns the response as first stored, even if the booking was changed or deleted since.
207	- **Intermediate attempts**: the worker reports after every attempt, so a booking whose attempt failed but has retries left shows `PENDING` with the number of attempts made so far.
208	- **How the worker learns the organizer address**: the job carries only the booking id and the worker has no database, so the worker asks the `booking` service for the booking; a booking that no longer exists ends the job without retries.
209	- **Updates and deletes do not notify**: changing or deleting a booking sends no new confirmation and does not cancel a pending one.
210	- **Queue failure after storing**: if the confirmation job cannot be enqueued, the booking is kept, the create answers 201, and the booking stays `PENDING`. No recovery mechanism is part of this feature.
211	- **Empty update**: an update with no fields is valid and changes nothing.
212	- **Web page times**: start and end are entered and shown in the browser's local time zone and sent to the API in UTC.
213	- **Web page paging**: the table shows 10 bookings per page with paging controls; the room filter and room names come from the first 100 rooms of the room list.
214	- **Delete confirmation**: the page asks the person to confirm before deleting a row.
215	- **New key rule on the page**: only a network error (no answer from the API) keeps the key for the next try; any answered request, or any change to the form, starts a new submission with a new key.
216	- **Dependencies**: the existing gateway, `booking`, `room` and `worker` services, their database, message bus and queue infrastructure, and the shared contract are used as they are; no new dependency is added.
217	- **Technical terms in this specification**: routes, status codes, error codes, header names and the queue name are part of the feature description's stated external behaviour and are kept verbatim so that the specification stays testable against the shared contract.
218

# Feature Specification: Meeting-Room Bookings

**Feature Branch**: none — no branch hook is installed; the work stays on `main` (feature directory `specs/001-room-bookings`)

**Created**: 2026-11-10

**Status**: Draft

**Input**: User description: "Add bookings to roombook: people book a meeting room for a time span, and get a confirmation." The description has four parts — a bookings API on the gateway, idempotent create, a confirmation job, and a `/bookings` page — plus a scope limit (the shared contract, the `room` service and the `/rooms` page are not changed) and a definition of done. Every rule it states is carried into this specification.

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Book a room and manage the booking (Priority: P1)

A person books a meeting room for a time span by giving the room, a title, the organizer's email, a start and an end. They can list bookings (all, or for one room), read one, change its title or times, and delete it.

**Why this priority**: Bookings are the feature. Every other story depends on a booking existing.

**Independent Test**: Through the gateway alone, create a booking for an existing room, list it, read it, change its end time, delete it, and confirm that reading it afterwards answers "not found".

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** an existing room, **When** a valid booking is created with a valid `Idempotency-Key`, **Then** the answer is 201 with the booking, whose `confirmationStatus` is `PENDING` and `confirmationAttempts` is 0.
2. **Given** bookings in several rooms, **When** the list is requested without `roomId`, **Then** the answer is `{ items, total, page, limit }` with all bookings ordered by `startsAt` ascending, 10 per page by default.
3. **Given** bookings in several rooms, **When** the list is requested with a `roomId`, **Then** only that room's bookings are counted and returned.
4. **Given** an existing booking, **When** it is read by id, **Then** the answer is 200 with the booking.
5. **Given** no booking with that id, **When** it is read, updated or deleted, **Then** the answer is 404 with `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`.
6. **Given** an existing booking, **When** its `title`, `startsAt` and/or `endsAt` are changed, **Then** the answer is 200 with the updated booking and a later `updatedAt`.
7. **Given** an existing booking, **When** it is deleted, **Then** the answer is 204 and reading it afterwards answers 404 with `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`.
8. **Given** a body with a missing or malformed field, **When** a create or update is requested, **Then** the answer is 400 and nothing is stored.
9. **Given** `endsAt` equal to or earlier than `startsAt`, **When** a booking is created, **Then** the answer is 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`.
10. **Given** an existing booking, **When** an update changes only one of the two times so that the stored pair would no longer have `endsAt` later than `startsAt`, **Then** the answer is 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` and the booking is unchanged.
11. **Given** a `roomId` that matches no room, **When** a booking is created, **Then** the answer is 404 with `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` and nothing is stored.

---

### User Story 2 - Retry a create safely (Priority: P2)

A client that is unsure whether its create request arrived can send it again with the same `Idempotency-Key` and never ends up with two bookings.

**Why this priority**: Without it, a network error during create leaves the client a choice between a possible duplicate and a possible lost booking.

**Independent Test**: Send the same create request twice with one key and observe one booking and an identical second answer marked as replayed; then vary the body, the key and the timing to observe each documented error.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a create request without an `Idempotency-Key` header, or with a value that is not a UUID, **When** it is sent, **Then** the answer is 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY` and nothing is stored.
2. **Given** a key that has not been used, **When** a valid create is sent, **Then** the booking is created and the key, a fingerprint of the request body and the response are stored together with it, all or nothing.
3. **Given** a completed create, **When** the same key is sent with the same body, **Then** the stored status and body are answered unchanged with the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`, no second booking exists and no second confirmation job is enqueued.
4. **Given** a completed create, **When** the booking is later updated or deleted and the same key and body are sent again, **Then** the originally stored answer is still returned unchanged.
5. **Given** a completed create, **When** the same key is sent with a different body, **Then** the answer is 422 with `UNPROCESSABLE.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.
6. **Given** a create that is still being processed, **When** the same key arrives again, **Then** the answer is 409 with `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`.
7. **Given** two identical create requests with the same key arriving at the same moment, **When** both are processed, **Then** exactly one booking exists; the other request is answered with either the replay or the 409.
8. **Given** a create that failed validation (invalid body, `endsAt` not later than `startsAt`, or unknown room), **When** the same key is sent again with a corrected body, **Then** it is treated as a first request and the booking is created.
9. **Given** a key used long ago, **When** it is sent again, **Then** it behaves exactly as above: keys do not expire.

---

### User Story 3 - Get a confirmation (Priority: P3)

After a booking is created, the organizer is "sent" a confirmation in the background, and the booking shows whether that succeeded and how many attempts it took.

**Why this priority**: It completes the promise "and get a confirmation", but a booking is already usable without it.

**Independent Test**: Create three bookings whose organizer addresses are an ordinary one, one at `@retry.example` and one at `@bounce.example`; after the retries have run, read each booking and compare its status and attempts with the fixed rules.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a newly created booking, **When** creation completes, **Then** exactly one confirmation job for that booking is on the `booking-confirmation` queue, with payload `{ bookingId }`, the job id `confirmationJobId(bookingId)`, 3 attempts and exponential backoff starting at 1 second.
2. **Given** an organizer address in any ordinary domain, **When** the job runs, **Then** the booking ends as `SENT` with 1 attempt.
3. **Given** an organizer address ending in `@retry.example`, **When** the job runs, **Then** the first two attempts fail, the third succeeds, and the booking ends as `SENT` with 3 attempts.
4. **Given** an organizer address ending in `@bounce.example`, **When** the job runs, **Then** every attempt fails and after the third the booking ends as `FAILED` with 3 attempts.
5. **Given** a booking whose confirmation already ended as `SENT` or `FAILED`, **When** the processor runs again for the same booking, **Then** the booking's status and attempts are unchanged.
6. **Given** the same attempt outcome is reported twice, **When** the second report arrives, **Then** the booking is in the same state as after the first.
7. **Given** a replayed create (User Story 2), **When** it is answered, **Then** the booking still has exactly one confirmation job.

---

### User Story 4 - Manage bookings from the web page (Priority: P4)

A person opens the Bookings page from the navigation, sees the bookings in a table, filters them by room, creates a booking with a form, and edits or deletes a row.

**Why this priority**: It is the human-facing surface of stories 1–3 and needs them to exist first.

**Independent Test**: With the service layer mocked, render the page and exercise the table, the filter, the create form, edit, delete, and the loading, empty and error states. Against a running system, do the same by hand at `/bookings`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** any page of the app, **When** the navigation is shown, **Then** it has a "Bookings" link that opens `/bookings`.
2. **Given** bookings exist, **When** the page loads, **Then** a table shows for each booking its title, room name, organizer, start, end and confirmation status.
3. **Given** the room list, **When** a room is chosen in the filter above the table, **Then** the table shows only that room's bookings; clearing the filter shows all of them again.
4. **Given** the create form filled with room, title, organizer email, start and end, **When** it is submitted successfully, **Then** the new booking appears in the table.
5. **Given** a submission that ended in a network error (no answer from the API), **When** the person retries the same submission, **Then** the request carries the same `Idempotency-Key` as the first try.
6. **Given** a submission that the API answered, successfully or with an error, **When** the form is submitted again, **Then** that is a new submission with a new `Idempotency-Key`.
7. **Given** a row, **When** its title, start or end is edited and saved, **Then** the row shows the updated values.
8. **Given** a row, **When** it is deleted and the deletion is confirmed, **Then** the row disappears from the table.
9. **Given** bookings are being fetched, **When** the page is shown, **Then** a loading state is visible.
10. **Given** there are no bookings (or none for the chosen room), **When** the page loads, **Then** an empty state is shown instead of an empty table.
11. **Given** the API answers an error to a load, create, edit or delete, **When** the page shows the failure, **Then** it shows the `message` from the API's error answer.

---

### Edge Cases

- **Header and body both invalid on create**: the idempotency key is checked first, so the answer is 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`.
- **Same key, different body, first request still in progress**: the body mismatch wins, so the answer is 422 with `UNPROCESSABLE.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.
- **Update with an empty body**: answered 200 with the booking unchanged.
- **Update that tries to change `roomId` or `organizerEmail`**: answered 400; only `title`, `startsAt` and `endsAt` can be changed.
- **An id in the path that is not a UUID**: answered 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`.
- **`page` below 1, `limit` below 1 or above 100, or a `roomId` filter that is not a UUID**: answered 400 with `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`.
- **A `roomId` filter for a room that does not exist**: answered 200 with an empty list; the filter does not check the room.
- **Two bookings for the same room at overlapping times**: both are accepted; this feature has no overlap rule.
- **A booking in the past**: accepted.
- **Booking deleted before its confirmation job runs or finishes**: the job ends quietly without further retries, and a late outcome report for the missing booking changes nothing.
- **The `room` service does not answer during create**: answered with `UNAVAILABLE.SERVICE`; nothing is stored and the key can be used again.
- **The queue is unreachable right after the booking is stored**: the create still answers 201 and the booking stays `PENDING`; recovering such a booking is outside this feature.
- **The form is edited after a network error**: the edited form is a new submission and gets a new `Idempotency-Key`.
- **More than one page of bookings on the web page**: the table offers paging at 10 per page.

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### Functional Requirements

**Bookings (gateway, under `/api`)**

- **FR-001**: The system MUST expose a booking as `id`, `roomId`, `title`, `organizerEmail`, `startsAt`, `endsAt`, `confirmationStatus` (`PENDING`, `SENT` or `FAILED`), `confirmationAttempts`, `createdAt` and `updatedAt`, with every time in ISO 8601 UTC.
- **FR-002**: `POST /api/bookings` MUST create a booking and answer 201 with it; a new booking MUST start with `confirmationStatus` `PENDING` and `confirmationAttempts` 0.
- **FR-003**: `GET /api/bookings` MUST answer `{ items, total, page, limit }` ordered by `startsAt` ascending, with `page` defaulting to 1, `limit` defaulting to 10 (maximum 100), and an optional `roomId` that restricts both `items` and `total` to that room.
- **FR-004**: `GET /api/bookings/:id` MUST answer 200 with the booking, or 404 with `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`.
- **FR-005**: `PATCH /api/bookings/:id` MUST change only `title`, `startsAt` and/or `endsAt` and answer 200 with the updated booking, or 404 with `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`.
- **FR-006**: `DELETE /api/bookings/:id` MUST answer 204, or 404 with `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING`; a deleted booking MUST be gone, so that reading it afterwards answers 404.
- **FR-007**: Every error MUST be answered as `{ statusCode, errorCode, message }` with `errorCode` taken from the shared contract.
- **FR-008**: An invalid body MUST be answered with 400 and store nothing. A title is 1 to 120 characters, `organizerEmail` is an email address, `roomId` is a UUID, and both times are strict ISO 8601.
- **FR-009**: `endsAt` MUST be later than `startsAt`; equal or earlier MUST be answered with 400 and `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`. After an update, the rule MUST hold for the resulting stored pair of times, including when only one of them was sent.
- **FR-010**: The room of a new booking MUST exist. The `booking` service MUST ask the `room` service, and an unknown room MUST be answered with 404 and `NOT_FOUND.ROOM`.
- **FR-011**: The `booking` service MUST own bookings and their storage. The gateway MUST only validate and forward; it holds no booking rules and no storage.

**Idempotent create**

- **FR-012**: `POST /api/bookings` MUST require the `Idempotency-Key` request header with a UUID value; a missing or non-UUID value MUST be answered with 400 and `BAD_REQUEST.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY`.
- **FR-013**: On the first request with a key, the system MUST store the key, a fingerprint of the request body, and the response. Claiming the key and inserting the booking MUST happen in one database transaction.
- **FR-014**: The same key with the same body, after the first request completed, MUST be answered with the stored status and body, unchanged, plus the response header `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; it MUST NOT create a second booking or enqueue a second confirmation job.
- **FR-015**: The same key with a different body MUST be answered with 422 and `UNPROCESSABLE.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`.
- **FR-016**: The same key while the first request is still being processed MUST be answered with 409 and `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`.
- **FR-017**: Two identical requests arriving at the same moment MUST never create two bookings.
- **FR-018**: A request that fails validation (FR-008, FR-009, FR-010) MUST NOT be stored against its key; the key MUST remain usable.
- **FR-019**: Idempotency keys MUST NOT expire.

**Confirmation job**

- **FR-020**: When a booking is created, the `booking` service MUST enqueue exactly one confirmation job on the queue `booking-confirmation` with payload `{ bookingId }`.
- **FR-021**: The job id MUST be `confirmationJobId(bookingId)`, so that a booking can never have two confirmation jobs.
- **FR-022**: The job MUST be given 3 attempts with exponential backoff starting at 1 second.
- **FR-023**: The `worker` service MUST process the job: it "sends" the confirmation and reports the outcome to the `booking` service over the message bus, and the `booking` service MUST update the booking's `confirmationStatus` and `confirmationAttempts`. The worker MUST NOT have database access.
- **FR-024**: Nothing MUST really be sent. The simulated sender MUST decide by the booking's `organizerEmail`:
  - ending in `@retry.example`: fail on attempts 1 and 2, succeed on attempt 3 — the booking ends as `SENT` with 3 attempts;
  - ending in `@bounce.example`: fail on every attempt — after the third the booking ends as `FAILED` with 3 attempts;
  - any other address: succeed on attempt 1 — `SENT` with 1 attempt.
- **FR-025**: The processor MUST be safe to run twice for the same booking: a repeated run or a repeated outcome report MUST NOT change a booking that already ended as `SENT` or `FAILED`, and MUST NOT lower `confirmationAttempts`.

**Bookings page (`apps/web`)**

- **FR-026**: The web app MUST have a `/bookings` page and a "Bookings" link in the navigation.
- **FR-027**: The page MUST show a table of bookings with title, room name, organizer, start, end and confirmation status.
- **FR-028**: The page MUST have a room filter above the table, filled from the room list.
- **FR-029**: The page MUST have a form to create a booking with room, title, organizer email, start and end.
- **FR-030**: Each form submission MUST generate one `Idempotency-Key`; a retry of the same submission after a network error MUST reuse that key.
- **FR-031**: Each row MUST offer edit (title, start, end) and delete.
- **FR-032**: The page MUST have loading, empty and error states; an error MUST show the `message` from the API.

**Scope and completion**

- **FR-033**: The shared contract (`libs/contract`), the `room` service and the `/rooms` page MUST NOT be changed. Every route name, message pattern, DTO class, error code, header name, queue name and constant MUST come from the shared contract as it is.
- **FR-034**: New and changed services MUST have unit tests, and the page MUST have tests with the service layer mocked.
- **FR-035**: `pnpm run build`, `pnpm run lint` and `pnpm run test` MUST pass.

### Key Entities

- **Booking**: one reservation of one room for a time span. Holds the room it is for, a title, the organizer's email, start and end, the state of its confirmation (status and number of attempts), and when it was created and last updated. Belongs to exactly one room; owned by the `booking` service.
- **Room**: an existing meeting room with a name and a capacity. Read-only for this feature; owned by the `room` service.
- **Idempotency record**: one per `Idempotency-Key`. Holds the key, the fingerprint of the request body it was first used with, whether that request is still in progress or completed, and the stored response (status and body). Never expires.
- **Confirmation job**: one background task per booking, identified by the booking, that drives the simulated sending with up to 3 attempts.
- **Confirmation outcome**: the report the worker gives the `booking` service after an attempt: the booking, the resulting status, and the attempt count.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

### Measurable Outcomes

- **SC-001**: A person can create, find, change and delete a booking, and 100% of the documented answers (success and error) match this specification when exercised end to end through the gateway.
- **SC-002**: Sending the same create request with the same key any number of times, one after another or at the same moment, results in exactly 1 booking and exactly 1 confirmation job, in 100% of trials.
- **SC-003**: Every replayed answer is identical in status and body to the original answer and is marked as replayed.
- **SC-004**: With the default retry timing, every booking reaches its final confirmation state within 10 seconds of creation: ordinary address `SENT` with 1 attempt, `@retry.example` `SENT` with 3 attempts, `@bounce.example` `FAILED` with 3 attempts.
- **SC-005**: Running the confirmation processor a second time for any booking leaves its status and attempts unchanged in 100% of trials.
- **SC-006**: On the Bookings page a person can create a booking in under 1 minute and can filter, edit and delete without leaving the page; every failure shows the API's own message.
- **SC-007**: The repository's build, lint and test commands all pass, and the `room` service, the `/rooms` page and the shared contract show no changes.

## Assumptions

- **No sign-in**: roombook has no authentication, so anyone who can reach the gateway or the page can create, change and delete any booking.
- **No overlap rule**: the description does not forbid two bookings of one room at the same time and the contract has no error code for it, so overlapping bookings are accepted.
- **Past bookings**: start and end may be in the past.
- **Invalid body error code**: "an invalid body answers 400" is answered with `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION`, the only general validation code in the contract. The same code is used for an invalid list query or a path id that is not a UUID.
- **"Fails validation" includes the room check**: the unknown-room answer is listed under validation in the description, so a 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` create is not stored against its key either.
- **"Same body"**: two bodies are the same when the five create fields (`roomId`, `title`, `organizerEmail`, `startsAt`, `endsAt`) have the same values; field order and whitespace in the JSON do not matter.
- **Mismatch before in-progress**: when a key is reused with a different body, the 422 applies whether or not the first request has completed.
- **Replay is a snapshot**: a replay returns the response as first stored, even if the booking was changed or deleted since.
- **Intermediate attempts**: the worker reports after every attempt, so a booking whose attempt failed but has retries left shows `PENDING` with the number of attempts made so far.
- **How the worker learns the organizer address**: the job carries only the booking id and the worker has no database, so the worker asks the `booking` service for the booking; a booking that no longer exists ends the job without retries.
- **Updates and deletes do not notify**: changing or deleting a booking sends no new confirmation and does not cancel a pending one.
- **Queue failure after storing**: if the confirmation job cannot be enqueued, the booking is kept, the create answers 201, and the booking stays `PENDING`. No recovery mechanism is part of this feature.
- **Empty update**: an update with no fields is valid and changes nothing.
- **Web page times**: start and end are entered and shown in the browser's local time zone and sent to the API in UTC.
- **Web page paging**: the table shows 10 bookings per page with paging controls; the room filter and room names come from the first 100 rooms of the room list.
- **Delete confirmation**: the page asks the person to confirm before deleting a row.
- **New key rule on the page**: only a network error (no answer from the API) keeps the key for the next try; any answered request, or any change to the form, starts a new submission with a new key.
- **Dependencies**: the existing gateway, `booking`, `room` and `worker` services, their database, message bus and queue infrastructure, and the shared contract are used as they are; no new dependency is added.
- **Technical terms in this specification**: routes, status codes, error codes, header names and the queue name are part of the feature description's stated external behaviour and are kept verbatim so that the specification stays testable against the shared contract.

**Feature**: `specs/001-room-bookings` | **Date**: 2026-11-10

Wire shapes are the classes in `libs/contract` and are not repeated here. This document covers what is
stored, the rules on it and the state changes.

## Booking — table `bookings`

Entity `BookingEntity` in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/entities/booking.entity.ts`. Owned by the
`booking` service.

| Column | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | `uuid` | primary key `PK_bookings_id`, default `gen_random_uuid()` |
| `room_id` | `uuid` | not null; no foreign key (see research R13) |
| `title` | `character varying(120)` | not null; 1–120 characters |
| `organizer_email` | `character varying(320)` | not null |
| `starts_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | not null |
| `ends_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | not null |
| `confirmation_status` | `character varying(10)` | not null, default `PENDING`; `CK_bookings_confirmation_status` limits it to `PENDING`, `SENT`, `FAILED` |
| `confirmation_attempts` | `integer` | not null, default 0 |
| `created_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | not null, default `now()` |
| `updated_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | not null, default `now()`; set on every change to the row |

Constraints and indexes:

- `CK_bookings_time_range`: `ends_at > starts_at`.
- `IDX_bookings_starts_at` on (`starts_at`, `id`) — the unfiltered list.
- `IDX_bookings_room_id_starts_at` on (`room_id`, `starts_at`, `id`) — the list filtered by room.

Mapping to `BookingDto`: column names become camelCase; the four times are answered with
`toISOString()`.

### Validation rules

| Rule | Enforced by | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| Field shapes (FR-008) | gateway validation pipe with `CreateBookingDto` / `UpdateBookingDto` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
| Unknown field on update | handler-level pipe on `PATCH` | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
| A time that does not parse to an instant | `booking` service | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
| `endsAt` later than `startsAt` on create (FR-009) | `booking` service; `CK_bookings_time_range` behind it | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
| Resulting pair valid on update (FR-009) | conditional update in the repository; the service chooses the answer | 400 `BAD_REQUEST.VALIDATION` |
| Room exists on create (FR-010) | `booking` service asks `room:findRoomById` | 404 `NOT_FOUND.ROOM` |
| Booking exists on read, update, delete | `booking` service | 404 `NOT_FOUND.BOOKING` |

### List

Ordered by `starts_at` ascending, then `id` ascending so pages are stable. `skip = (page - 1) * limit`,
`take = limit`. An optional `roomId` restricts both the rows and the total.

### Confirmation state

```text
                 report SENT (attempts n)
   PENDING ───────────────────────────────▶ SENT      (final)
     │  ▲
     │  └── report PENDING (attempts n)     attempts rises, status stays
     │
     └──────────────────────────────────▶ FAILED    (final)
                 report FAILED (attempts 3)
```

A report is applied only when the stored status is `PENDING` and the stored attempts are not greater
than the reported attempts. Consequences:

- `SENT` and `FAILED` never change.
- `confirmation_attempts` never goes down.
- The same report applied twice leaves the same state.
- A report for a booking that no longer exists changes nothing.

Updating or deleting a booking does not touch its confirmation state and does not create or cancel a
job.

## Idempotency record — table `idempotency_keys`

Entity `IdempotencyKeyEntity` in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/entities/idempotency-key.entity.ts`.
Owned by the `booking` service.

| Column | Type | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `key` | `uuid` | primary key `PK_idempotency_keys_key`; the `Idempotency-Key` value |
| `request_fingerprint` | `character(64)` | not null; sha256 hex of the five create fields in a fixed order |
| `response_status` | `smallint` | not null; the stored HTTP status (201) |
| `response_body` | `jsonb` | not null; the `BookingDto` answered by the first request |
| `created_at` | `timestamp with time zone` | not null, default `now()` |

Rules:

- A row is written only in the same transaction that inserts the booking, so a row always means a
  completed create. There is no status column: "in progress" is the open claim transaction, held as
  two transaction-scoped advisory locks (research R3).
- No foreign key to `bookings`: the stored answer must survive the booking being updated or deleted
  (replay is a snapshot).
- Rows are never deleted or expired (FR-019).
- Failed validation, an unknown room and an unavailable `room` service store nothing (FR-018).

### Claim outcomes

The repository's claim returns one outcome; the service maps it to the answer.

| Outcome | Condition | Answer |
|---|---|---|
| `CREATED` | no row for the key; booking and row inserted | 201 with the booking; job enqueued |
| `REPLAYED` | row with the same fingerprint | stored status and body, `Idempotency-Replayed: true`; nothing enqueued |
| `KEY_REUSED` | row with another fingerprint, or the key is being claimed with another body | 422 `UNPROCESSABLE.IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` |
| `IN_PROGRESS` | the same key and body are being claimed now | 409 `CONFLICT.IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` |

## Room — table `rooms` (read-only)

Existing `RoomEntity`, owned by the `room` service. Not changed. The `booking` service reads a room
only through `room:findRoomById`; the web page reads rooms only through `GET /api/rooms`.

## Confirmation job — queue `booking-confirmation` (Redis, not Postgres)

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Job name | `QueueEnum.BOOKING_CONFIRMATION` (the contract defines no job name) |
| Job id | `confirmationJobId(bookingId)` |
| Payload | `ConfirmationJobDto` — `{ bookingId }` |
| Attempts | `CONFIRMATION_JOB_ATTEMPTS` (3) |
| Backoff | exponential, `CONFIRMATION_BACKOFF_MS` (1000 ms) |
| Retention | kept after completion or failure, so a second `add` with the same id is ignored |

## Confirmation outcome — message, not stored

`RecordConfirmationResultDto` — `{ bookingId, status, attempts }`, sent by the worker on
`booking:recordConfirmationResult` after every attempt.

| Organizer address | Attempt 1 | Attempt 2 | Attempt 3 | Final booking |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ends in `@retry.example` | `PENDING`, 1 | `PENDING`, 2 | `SENT`, 3 | `SENT`, 3 |
| ends in `@bounce.example` | `PENDING`, 1 | `PENDING`, 2 | `FAILED`, 3 | `FAILED`, 3 |
| any other | `SENT`, 1 | — | — | `SENT`, 1 |

## Migrations

Added in `libs/backend-common/src/lib/database/migrations/` and registered in `index.ts`:

- `1731200000002-create-bookings.ts`
- `1731200000003-create-idempotency-keys.ts`

Both entities are added to `data-source.ts` and exported from `libs/backend-common/src/index.ts`.
